statement: The inverse Laplace transform of a function F(s) is a real function f(t) that is piecewise-continuous and exponentially restricted (|f(t)| <= M * e^(alpha * t) for all t >= 0, for constants M > 0 and alpha in R) such that L{f}(s) = F(s), where L denotes the Laplace transform. The supplied source genuinely contains nothing to derive, stating definitions and inversion formulas (Bromwich's and Post's inversion formulas) without derivation steps.

properties.property: Uniqueness under Lerch's theorem: if F has an inverse Laplace transform f, f is uniquely determined up to a point set of Lebesgue measure zero
properties.why: Functions differing only on a set of Lebesgue measure zero possess identical Laplace transforms

properties.property: Bromwich's inversion formula: f(t) = L^-1{F(s)}(t) = (1 / (2 * pi * i)) * lim_{T -> infinity} int_{gamma - i*T}^{gamma + i*T} e^(s*t) * F(s) ds
properties.why: Integrates along a vertical line Re(s) = gamma located to the right of all singularities of F where F is bounded

properties.property: Equivalence of Bromwich's formula to the inverse Fourier transform when all singularities satisfy Re(s_k) < 0 or F is entire
properties.why: The contour line Re(s) = gamma can be set to gamma = 0, which aligns the contour with the imaginary axis
Bromwich's complex line integral is evaluated in practice by closing the contour and summing residues at the enclosed singularities

properties.property: Post's inversion formula: f(t) = L^-1{F}(t) = lim_{k -> infinity} ((-1)^k / k!) * (k / t)^(k + 1) * F^(k)(k / t) for t > 0
properties.why: Expresses the inverse transform as an asymptotic limit of high-order derivatives of F without requiring the locations of poles

assumptions.assumption: f(t) is piecewise-continuous on [0, infinity) and exponentially restricted (|f(t)| <= M * e^(alpha * t) for all t >= 0 with M > 0, alpha in R)
assumptions.breaks_when: f(t) grows super-exponentially (e.g., e^(t^2)) or has infinite/essential discontinuities on [0, infinity)

assumptions.assumption: In Bromwich's formula, the vertical line Re(s) = gamma satisfies gamma > Re(s_k) for all singularities s_k of F, and F is bounded on that line
assumptions.breaks_when: gamma is less than or equal to the real part of any singularity of F, the path lies outside the region of convergence, or F is unbounded along the line

assumptions.assumption: In Post's formula, f is continuous on [0, infinity) of exponential order (sup_{t > 0} f(t)/e^(b*t) < infinity for some b in R) and s > b
assumptions.breaks_when: f is discontinuous, f grows faster than any exponential function, or evaluation occurs at s <= b

failure_modes.mode: Contour misplacement or divergence of the Bromwich line integral
failure_modes.signature: The complex line integral diverges or fails to recover f(t)
failure_modes.cause: gamma is chosen such that gamma <= Re(s_k) for some singularity s_k of F, or F is unbounded along Re(s) = gamma

failure_modes.mode: Computational and algebraic intractability in Post's inversion formula
failure_modes.signature: Inability to analytically or numerically compute the inverse transform
failure_modes.cause: Post's formula requires computing derivatives F^(k) of arbitrarily high orders k as k -> infinity

failure_modes.mode: Indeterminacy on sets of measure zero
failure_modes.signature: Values of f(t) at isolated points or jump discontinuities are not uniquely pinned down
failure_modes.cause: Lerch's theorem only guarantees uniqueness up to sets having Lebesgue measure zero
